name: x3270
desc: IBM 3270 terminal emulator for the X Window System and Windows
why: An IBM 3270 mainframe terminal emulator, a window into a decades-old protocol and a whole old-school computing world.

brief.what_it_is: x3270 is an IBM 3270 terminal emulator for the X Window System and Windows. It runs over a TELNET connection and emulates either an IBM 3279 (color) or 3278 (monochrome) terminal, so it lets a desktop act as a mainframe terminal. It runs on most Unix-like systems, including Linux, macOS, Solaris and Cygwin, and natively on Windows. It is distributed as source code and is free to use. The homepage describes several front ends: x3270 (X display), wx3270 (Windows GUI), c3270 (curses, for dumb terminals and consoles), wc3270 (Windows console), s3270 (displayless, for screen-scraping scripts), tcl3270 (s3270 integrated with Tcl), and pr3287 (printer emulation). It also mentions x026, an IBM 026 keypunch emulator.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It presents x3270 as a way to reach IBM 3270 mainframe applications over TN3270/TELNET from Unix, X and Windows machines.
brief.how_it_works: It connects over TELNET and speaks the 3270 data stream, including the full TN3270E protocol, with optional SSL/TLS via OpenSSL. Beyond interactive use it offers printer session integration, IND$FILE file transfer, a pop-up keypad for 3270-specific keys, and scripting and debugging facilities. The s3270 variant has no display and is meant for scripts that read screens. The homepage says it does not yet support graphics.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has no install instructions. It links to Download, Documentation and Credits pages, which I did not follow. The homepage says it is distributed as source code, so a source build is implied for Unix-like systems. Windows has a native build (wx3270, wc3270). Nothing on the homepage mentions accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration. The brew executables list suggests the package installs b3270, c3270, pr3287, prtodir, s3270, x3270, x3270a and x3270if, but the homepage does not document them.
brief.standout: It is one of the few open-source emulators that covers the full 3270 family, including TN3270E, IND$FILE transfer, APL2 and DBCS (Chinese and Japanese) character sets, and a scripting-oriented headless variant (s3270) alongside the GUI and curses front ends. Its scripting and screen-scraping angle is the part that differs most from simple terminal emulators.
brief.status: maintained, with weak evidence: the homepage shows a news entry dated 2025-11-23 reading 'Webpage updated', and a 2020-03-17 entry for the x3270 Wiki launch. The homepage shows no software release date, and I did not check the Download page or a repository.
brief.caveats: No graphics support, which the homepage states outright. Licensing is not described on the homepage (a License link exists but I did not follow it), so check it before redistributing. The homepage does not describe build requirements beyond the OpenSSL reference. Only the homepage was read; the Documentation, Download and Wiki pages were not followed. The scout note's description matches the homepage. The brew-caveats field was empty.
quotes: x3270 is an IBM 3270 terminal emulator for the X Window System and Windows.
x3270 is distributed as source code, and can be used for free.
It does not yet support graphics.
Comments and questions about x3270 should be directed to Paul Mattes.
fetch_log: https://x3270.bgp.nu/ - fetched OK; returned homepage text with feature list, variant list and news. Nav links (Screenshots, Documentation, License, Download, Credits) not followed.

judge.reason: x3270 exposes the alien, host-driven 3270 protocol—including headless scripted sessions—rather than merely offering another terminal emulator.

entry.title: x3270
entry.tldr: A terminal emulator for IBM 3270 mainframe screens, with GUI, curses and headless variants, so a modern desktop can talk to a mainframe over TELNET.
entry.deeper_look:
x3270 emulates the IBM 3279 (color) and 3278 (monochrome) terminals. It connects over TELNET and speaks the 3270 data stream, including TN3270E, with optional SSL/TLS through OpenSSL. The result is that a Unix, macOS or Windows machine can sit in front of a mainframe application the way a dedicated terminal once did.

The package is a family of front ends. x3270 is the X window version, c3270 runs in curses on a plain console, and s3270 has no display at all and is meant for scripts that read screens. pr3287 emulates a 3287 printer session. The homepage also mentions IND$FILE file transfer, a pop-up keypad for 3270-specific keys, APL2 and DBCS (Chinese and Japanese) character sets, and scripting and debugging facilities.

The idea underneath is that a 3270 terminal is not a character stream like a Unix tty. The host sends whole screens made of fields, and the terminal sends back the fields that changed. That block-oriented model is why s3270 can work as a screen-scraping tool: a script reads a screen, fills in fields and presses a key. It is a door into how mainframe interactive computing worked, and still works.

The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It simply presents the tool as a way to reach IBM 3270 applications over TN3270 from Unix, X and Windows machines.
entry.install:
brew install x3270
# You need a TN3270 host to connect to. The brief does not say whether one is bundled or public.
# x3270 needs an X display, so on macOS you will need XQuartz. c3270 works in any terminal.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the options for the curses front end, which runs in an ordinary terminal with no X display.
Shows the options for the displayless, scriptable variant used for screen scraping.
Lists the options for the X window front end, the full graphical emulator.

entry.whats_unique: It is one of the few open-source emulators covering the whole 3270 family, with TN3270E, IND$FILE and DBCS support. The headless s3270 variant sets it apart from ordinary terminal emulators.
entry.caveats: It does not support graphics, the homepage lists no commands to get started, and you need a TN3270 host to connect to for it to do anything.
